section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "Return O Israel until Hashem your G-d," interpreting "until" as a term of eternity within the realm of time, relating to Malchus, and connecting the sevenfold recitation of "Hashem is the Elokim" on Yom Kippur to both the ascent to Atzmus Ein Sof and the subsequent descent of influence.
section.t: And this is [the meaning of] "Return O Israel until Hashem your G-d,"
"until" is a term of eternity,
for the concept of eternity applies specifically within the category of time
(for that which is above the category of time is above even the state of past, present, and future being as one),
except that within the category of time it is in a manner of eternity.
Therefore, "until" is in the aspect of Malchus,
which is
in the aspect and category of time.
And "Israel" is the aspect of Zeir Anpin.
And the explanation of "Return O Israel until Hashem your G-d" is
that one must bring back Israel until Malchus is in the manner of "until," and the aspects of Israel and the aspect of "until"
(Zeir Anpin and Malchus,
aspects of the chain of descent)
[become] "to Hashem your G-d,"
meaning to the Atzmus of Ein Sof, relative to Whom "Hashem is considered as Elokim,"
and from there one must draw down into the aspect of "Hashem your G-d,"
"Hashem" being a term that brings into being, and in this itself, as it is clothed in the Name Elokim,
and becomes "your G-d," your strength and your vitality.
And this is also the meaning of what we say at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, seven times, "Hashem is the Elokim,"
for within the Ten Days of Repentance themselves
[when repentance is most beautiful and is accepted immediately]
the essence of repentance is on Yom Kippur,
as the Rambam states,
"Yom Kippur is the time of repentance for all... and it is the end of pardon and forgiveness for Israel...,"
and within Yom Kippur itself, the essence of repentance is at the Neilah prayer
(the closing of the day)
for then is the closing of the gates, and Israel and the King are alone together,
therefore we then say seven times "Hashem is the Elokim,"
which contains these two concepts.
The concept of ascent
(from below to above)
into the Atzmus of Ein Sof,
and it is known that the concept of "Hashem is the Elokim"
(which we say at the Neilah of Yom Kippur)
is that Zeir Anpin
(Hashem)
in its ascent to Atik is "considered as Elokim,"
and the concept of drawing down from above to below
(in "Hashem" a term that brings into being, and "until" as it is clothed in the Name Elokim),
for this is why we say this seven times, in order to draw down into the aspect of the seven lower Sefiros.

And it can be said that this is also the meaning of what we say then: "Shema Yisrael Hashem Elokeinu Hashem Echad" once, "Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuso LeOlam VaEd" three times, and "Hashem is the Elokim" seven times,
"Shema Yisrael..." once is the matter of ascent from below to above,
and "Baruch Shem Kevod Malchuso LeOlam VaEd"
three times, and "Hashem is the Elokim" seven times is the matter of drawing down from above to below in all ten Sefiros
(three intellective faculties and seven emotive attributes).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the concept of two half-forms of the trumpets to the level of revelation where the Holy One and the Jewish people are two halves, contrasting it with the level of Atzmus where they are truly one, and explains the superiority of the shofar over trumpets as it stems from the essence of the soul which is one with the Essence.
section.t: And this can be connected to the verse, "And on your joyous days... and you shall sound the trumpets...,"
and the teaching of the Maggid of Mezeritch is known,
"Two trumpets, two half-forms,"
and it is explained in the maamar
that the concept of two half-forms is in the aspect of revelations
(form indicates revelation),
where it is applicable to say that the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Congregation of Israel are two half-forms that complete each other.
However, regarding the Essence,
Israel and the Holy One, blessed be He, are truly one
(and it is not applicable to say they are two halves).
And likewise, this is also the case regarding the two half-forms in the soul,
the part of the soul that is the "upper head" of the soul and the part of the soul that is in the body
(the aspect of Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah)
the "foot" of the soul,
for this is specifically in the aspect of the revelations of the soul,
for even the "head" of the soul is up to the aspect of Chayah, which has a connection to the aspect of the "foot" of the soul
(the soul within the body),
therefore it is called "Mazal" because it drips and flows down the illumination of the soul that is clothed in the body.
However, regarding the aspect of Yechidah, and especially the essence of the soul,
even though it includes all the powers and, on a higher level, carries all the powers,
it is above the aspect of a source and connection to the aspect of revelations,
and it
(specifically)
is found in all the aspects of the soul,
even in its aspect of "heel,"
and also in the "heel" of the body,
and also in the four cubits
(that are outside the human body),
therefore a person's four cubits acquire for him,
as explained in many places,
and this is the superiority of the shofar over the trumpets,
as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said,
"The shofar lengthens and the trumpets shorten, for the mitzvah of the day is with the shofar,"
for the service of the shofar is with the essence of the soul, which is truly one with the Essence,
above
the concept of two half-forms.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the shofar's "lengthening" refers to reaching the Essence both above and below, thereby fulfilling the purpose of a dwelling place for His Essence in the lower realms, while the trumpets are still needed for the aspect of revealed vessels, though the primary mitzvah of Rosh Hashanah is the shofar.
section.t: And this is also [the meaning of] "the shofar lengthens,"
for the concept of lengthening is both above and below,
because the service of the shofar reaches the Essence
(the essence of the soul and His Essence, blessed be He)
which is above all revelations
(lengthening above),
and which, as mentioned, is also found in the "heel"
(lengthening below),
and through this the intention of a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms is completed,
in both aspects,
"for Him" [meaning] for His Essence, and "in the lower realms."
However, the aspect of revelations is also necessary,
and just as in the dwelling of a mortal king, there must be
(in addition to the main point,
a dwelling for the essence of the king)
a beautiful dwelling and beautiful vessels,
therefore trumpets are also necessary,
and due to the endearment in this, both sounds are heard
(trumpets and shofar),
but the mitzvah of the day is with the shofar,
because the essence of the service on Rosh Hashanah is the service that stems from the essence of the soul, which is one with the Essence.
